# pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-pango-bindings)Rust Pango bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [Pango](https://docs.gtk.org/Pango/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

Pango **1.40** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
pango = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "pango" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
pango = "0.13"
pango = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "pango" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#see-also)See Also

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**pango** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

# pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-pango-bindings)Rust Pango bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [Pango](https://docs.gtk.org/Pango/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

Pango **1.40** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
pango = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "pango" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
pango = "0.13"
pango = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "pango" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#see-also)See Also

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**pango** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

- [ATTR_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.ATTR_INDEX_FROM_TEXT_BEGINNING.html)- INDEX_ - FROM_ - TEXT_ - BEGINNING
- Value for @start_index in `Attribute`
- [ATTR_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.ATTR_INDEX_TO_TEXT_END.html)- INDEX_ - TO_ - TEXT_ - END
- Value for @end_index in `Attribute`
- [GLYPH_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.GLYPH_EMPTY.html)- EMPTY
- A `PangoGlyph`value that indicates a zero-width empty glpyh.
- [GLYPH_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.GLYPH_INVALID_INPUT.html)- INVALID_ - INPUT
- A `PangoGlyph`value for invalid input.
- [GLYPH_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.GLYPH_UNKNOWN_FLAG.html)- UNKNOWN_ - FLAG
- Flag used in `PangoGlyph`to turn a`gunichar`value of a valid Unicode character into an unknown-character glyph for that`gunichar`.
- [SCALE](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.SCALE.html)
- The scale between dimensions used for Pango distances and device units.
- [SCALE_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.SCALE_LARGE.html)- LARGE
- The scale factor for one magnification step (1.2).
- [SCALE_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.SCALE_MEDIUM.html)- MEDIUM
- The scale factor for normal size (1.0).
- [SCALE_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.SCALE_SMALL.html)- SMALL
- The scale factor for one shrinking step (1 / 1.2).
- [SCALE_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.SCALE_XX_LARGE.html)- XX_ - LARGE
- The scale factor for three magnification steps (1.2 * 1.2 * 1.2).
- [SCALE_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.SCALE_XX_SMALL.html)- XX_ - SMALL
- The scale factor for three shrinking steps (1 / (1.2 * 1.2 * 1.2)).
- [SCALE_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.SCALE_X_LARGE.html)- X_ - LARGE
- The scale factor for two magnification steps (1.2 * 1.2).
- [SCALE_](https://gtk-rs.org/constant.SCALE_X_SMALL.html)- X_ - SMALL
- The scale factor for two shrinking steps (1 / (1.2 * 1.2)).

# pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/git/docs/pango

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-pango-bindings)Rust Pango bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [Pango](https://docs.gtk.org/Pango/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

Pango **1.40** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
pango = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "pango" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
pango = "0.13"
pango = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "pango" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#see-also)See Also

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**pango** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

# Unlocking the GNOME stack for Rust – gtk-rs

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/

#

          Unlocking the GNOME stack for Rust [§](https://gtk-rs.org#unlocking-the-gnome-stack-for-rust)

The **gtk-rs** project provides safe bindings to the [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org) language for fundamental libraries from the [GNOME](https://developer.gnome.org/components/) stack like [GLib](https://developer.gnome.org/glib), [Cairo](https://cairographics.org/documentation/), and [GTK 4](https://gtk.org).

##

##

          The introductory book [§](https://gtk-rs.org#the-introductory-book)

  Julian Hofer is writing a book titled [GUI development with Rust and GTK 4](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/book). We recommend both new and experienced **gtk-rs** users to have a look at it. While this book is targeted at people who want to develop GTK 4 applications, it also covers more general aspects of the GNOME stack such as **GObject Concepts**, **The Main Event Loop** and **GSettings**.

##

          The gtk-rs ecosystem [§](https://gtk-rs.org#the-gtk-rs-ecosystem)

By now, a number of additional bindings for GObject based libraries exist. While not part of the gtk-rs project, many of them are developed in close collaboration. Notable other projects within the gtk-rs ecosystem are

- **GStreamer**Open source multimedia framework
- **Adwaita**Building blocks for modern GNOME applications
- **SourceView 5**A library extending GtkTextView with features typical for a source code editor
- **Relm 4**An idiomatic GUI library inspired by Elm and based on gtk4-rs

More bindings can be found as part of the [GNOME GitLab Rust Group](https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Rust).

All these bindings are generated on the basis of GObject introspection (GIR). The book [Generate Rust bindings for GIR based libraries](https://gtk-rs.org/gir/book/) provides the documentation for the tools that gtk-rs provides to generate such bindings.

# glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-glib-and-gobject-bindings)Rust GLib and GObject bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [GLib](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

GLib **2.56** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

This library contains bindings to GLib and GObject types and APIs as well as common building blocks used in both handmade and machine generated bindings to GTK and other GLib-based libraries.

It is the foundation for higher level libraries with uniform Rusty (safe and strongly typed) APIs. It avoids exposing GLib-specific data types where possible and is not meant to provide comprehensive GLib bindings, which would often amount to duplicating the Rust Standard Library or other utility crates.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dynamic-typing)Dynamic typing

Most types in the GLib family have [ Type](https://gtk-rs.org/types/struct.Type.html) identifiers.
Their corresponding Rust types implement the

[trait.](https://gtk-rs.org/types/trait.StaticType.html)

`StaticType`A dynamically typed [ Value](https://gtk-rs.org/value/struct.Value.html) can carry values of any

`StaticType`.
[Variants](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/variant/struct.Variant.html)can carry values of

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/variant/trait.StaticVariantType.html)

`StaticVariantType`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#errors)Errors

Errors are represented by [ Error](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.Error.html), which can
carry values from various

[error domains](https://gtk-rs.org/error/trait.ErrorDomain.html)such as

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html)

`FileError`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#objects)Objects

Each class and interface has a corresponding smart pointer struct
representing an instance of that type (e.g. [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) for

[or](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/class.Object.html)

`GObject`[for](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk4/struct.Widget.html)

`gtk4::Widget`[). They are reference counted and feature interior mutability similarly to Rust’s](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Widget.html)

`GtkWidget`[idiom. Consequently, cloning objects is cheap and their methods never require mutable borrows. Two smart pointers are equal if they point to the same object.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cell/index.html#introducing-mutability-inside-of-something-immutable)

`Rc<RefCell<T>>`The root of the object hierarchy is [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html).
Inheritance and subtyping is denoted with the

[marker trait. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.IsA.html)

`IsA`[trait enables upcasting and downcasting.](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.Cast.html)

`Cast`Interfaces and non-leaf classes also have corresponding traits (e.g.
[ ObjectExt](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.ObjectExt.html) or

[), which are blanketly implemented for all their subtypes.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk4/prelude/trait.WidgetExt.html)

`WidgetExt`You can create new subclasses of [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) or other object types. Look at
the module’s documentation for further details and a code example.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#under-the-hood)Under the hood

GLib-based libraries largely operate on pointers to various boxed or
reference counted structures so the bindings have to implement corresponding
smart pointers (wrappers), which encapsulate resource management and safety
checks. Such wrappers are defined via the
[ wrapper!](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.wrapper.html) macro, which uses abstractions
defined in the

[,](https://gtk-rs.org/wrapper/index.html)

`wrapper`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/boxed/index.html)

`boxed`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/shared/index.html)

`shared`[modules. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/index.html)

`object`[module defines and partly implements conversions between high level Rust types (including the aforementioned wrappers) and their FFI counterparts.](https://gtk-rs.org/translate/index.html)

`translate`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
glib = "0.13"
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**glib** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

## Structs[§](https://gtk-rs.org#structs)

- [Binding](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Binding.html)
- `GObject`instance (or source) and another property on another- `GObject`instance (or target).
- [Binding](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.BindingFlags.html)- Flags
- Flags to be passed to g_object_bind_property() or g_object_bind_property_full().
- [Binding](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.BindingGroup.html)- Group - `v2_72`
- `GBindingGroup`can be used to bind multiple properties from an object collectively.
- [Binding](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.BindingGroupBuilder.html)- Group - Builder - `v2_72`
- Builder for binding group bindings.
- [Bookmark](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.BookmarkFile.html)- File - `v2_76`
- GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.
- [Boxed](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.BoxedAnyObject.html)- AnyObject
- This is a subclass of `glib::object::Object`capable of storing any Rust type. It let’s you insert a Rust type anywhere a`glib::object::Object`is needed. The inserted value can then be borrowed as a Rust type, by using the various provided methods.
- [Byte](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ByteArray.html)- Array
- Contains the public fields of a `GByteArray`.
- [Bytes](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Bytes.html)
- A shared immutable byte slice (the equivalent of `Rc<[u8]>`).
- [Checksum](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Checksum.html)
- GLib provides a generic API for computing checksums (or ‘digests’) for a sequence of arbitrary bytes, using various hashing algorithms like MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256. Checksums are commonly used in various environments and specifications.
- [Collation](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.CollationKey.html)- Key
- A `CollationKey`allows ordering strings using the linguistically correct rules for the current locale.
- [Date](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Date.html)
- GLib type: Inline allocated boxed type with stack copy semantics.
- [Date](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.DateTime.html)- Time
- `GDateTime`is a structure that combines a Gregorian date and time into a single structure.
- [Exit](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ExitCode.html)- Code
- [File](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FileSetContentsFlags.html)- SetContents - Flags - `v2_66`
- Flags to pass to g_file_set_contents_full() to affect its safety and performance.

So for collection of short int or char,- `'i'`needs to be used, and for collection of floats- `'d'`. The #GTypeValueTable provides the functions required by the #GValue implementation, to serve as a container for values of a type.

- The kind of decomposition to perform
- [File](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html)- Error
- Values corresponding to @errno codes returned from file operations on UNIX. Unlike @errno codes, GFileError values are available on all systems, even Windows. The exact meaning of each code depends on what sort of file operation you were performing; the UNIX documentation gives more details. The following error code descriptions come from the GNU C Library manual, and are under the copyright of that manual.
- [GStr](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.GStrError.html)- Error

- [LogLevel](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.LogLevel.html)
- [LogWriter](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.LogWriterOutput.html)- Output
- Return values from #GLogWriterFuncs to indicate whether the given log entry was successfully handled by the writer, or whether there was an error in handling it (and hence a fallback writer should be used).
- [Markup](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.MarkupError.html)- Error
- Error codes returned by markup parsing.
- [Normalize](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.NormalizeMode.html)- Mode
- Defines how a Unicode string is transformed in a canonical form, standardizing such issues as whether a character with an accent is represented as a base character and combining accent or as a single precomposed character. Unicode strings should generally be normalized before comparing them.
- [Option](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.OptionArg.html)- Arg
- The #GOptionArg enum values determine which type of extra argument the
options expect to find. If an option expects an extra argument, it can
be specified in several ways; with a short option: `-x arg`, with a long option:`--name arg`or combined in a single argument:`--name=arg`.
- [Seek](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.SeekType.html)- Type
- An enumeration specifying the base position for a g_io_channel_seek_position() operation.
- [Time](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TimeType.html)- Type
- Disambiguates a given time in two ways.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeBreakType.html)- Break - Type
- These are the possible line break classifications.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeScript.html)- Script
- The #GUnicodeScript enumeration identifies different writing systems. The values correspond to the names as defined in the Unicode standard. The enumeration has been added in GLib 2.14, and is interchangeable with #PangoScript.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeType.html)- Type

Unicode specification.

- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_VERSION.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - VERSION
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the version of the Desktop Entry Specification used for the desktop entry file.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_APPLICATION.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - APPLICATION
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing applications.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_DIRECTORY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - DIRECTORY
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing directories.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_LINK.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - LINK
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing links to documents.
- [OPTION_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.OPTION_REMAINING.html)- REMAINING
- If a long option in the main group has this name, it is not treated as a
regular option. Instead it collects all non-option arguments which would
otherwise be left in `argv`. The option must be of type`OptionArg::Callback``OptionArg::StringArray``OptionArg::FilenameArray`
- [STR_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.STR_DELIMITERS.html)- DELIMITERS
- The standard delimiters, used in `strdelimit()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_ISOLATE_DIRS.html)- OPTION_ - ISOLATE_ - DIRS - `v2_60`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_NONFATAL_ASSERTIONS.html)- OPTION_ - NONFATAL_ - ASSERTIONS - `v2_84`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_NO_PRGNAME.html)- OPTION_ - NO_ - PRGNAME - `v2_84`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [URI_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.URI_RESERVED_CHARS_GENERIC_DELIMITERS.html)- RESERVED_ - CHARS_ - GENERIC_ - DELIMITERS
- Generic delimiters characters as defined in
[RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986). Includes`:/?#[]@`.
- [URI_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.URI_RESERVED_CHARS_SUBCOMPONENT_DELIMITERS.html)- RESERVED_ - CHARS_ - SUBCOMPONENT_ - DELIMITERS
- Subcomponent delimiter characters as defined in
[RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986). Includes`!$&'()*+,;=`.

## Functions[§](https://gtk-rs.org#functions)

- [access](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.access.html)
- A wrapper for the POSIX access() function. This function is used to test a pathname for one or several of read, write or execute permissions, or just existence.
- [application_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.application_name.html)- name
- Gets a human-readable name for the application, as set by
g_set_application_name(). This name should be localized if
possible, and is intended for display to the user.  Contrast with
g_get_prgname(), which gets a non-localized name. If
g_set_application_name() has not been called, returns the result of
g_get_prgname() (which may be `None`
- [base64_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.base64_decode.html)- decode
- Decode a sequence of Base-64 encoded text into binary data. Note that the returned binary data is not necessarily zero-terminated, so it should not be used as a character string.
- [base64_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.base64_encode.html)- encode
- Encode a sequence of binary data into its Base-64 stringified representation.

- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_checksum_for_data.html)- checksum_ - for_ - data

- Converts a string from one character set to another.
- [convert_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.convert_with_fallback.html)- with_ - fallback
- Converts a string from one character set to another, possibly including fallback sequences for characters not representable in the output. Note that it is not guaranteed that the specification for the fallback sequences in @fallback will be honored. Some systems may do an approximate conversion from @from_codeset to @to_codeset in their iconv() functions, in which case GLib will simply return that approximate conversion.
- [current_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.current_dir.html)- dir
- Gets the current directory.
- [dcgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dcgettext.html)
- This is a variant of g_dgettext() that allows specifying a locale
category instead of always using `LC_MESSAGES`. See g_dgettext() for more information about how this functions differs from calling dcgettext() directly.
- [dgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dgettext.html)
- This function is a wrapper of dgettext() which does not translate the message if the default domain as set with textdomain() has no translations for the current locale.
- [dngettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dngettext.html)
- This function is a wrapper of dngettext() which does not translate the message if the default domain as set with textdomain() has no translations for the current locale.
- [dpgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dpgettext.html)
- This function is a variant of g_dgettext() which supports a disambiguating message context. GNU gettext uses the ‘\004’ character to separate the message context and message id in @msgctxtid. If 0 is passed as @msgidoffset, this function will fall back to trying to use the deprecated convention of using “|” as a separation character.
- [dpgettext2](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dpgettext2.html)
- This function is a variant of g_dgettext() which supports a disambiguating message context. GNU gettext uses the ‘\004’ character to separate the message context and message id in @msgctxtid.
- [environ](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.environ.html)
- Gets the list of environment variables for the current process.
- [environ_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.environ_getenv.html)- getenv
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_get_contents.html)- get_ - contents
- Reads an entire file into allocated memory, with good error checking.
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_open_tmp.html)- open_ - tmp - Unix
- Opens a file for writing in the preferred directory for temporary files (as returned by g_get_tmp_dir()).
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_set_contents.html)- set_ - contents
- Writes all of @contents to a file named @filename. This is a convenience
wrapper around calling g_file_set_contents_full() with `flags`set to`G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_CONSISTENT | G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_ONLY_EXISTING`and`mode`set to`0666`.
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_set_contents_full.html)- set_ - contents_ - full - `v2_66`
- Writes all of @contents to a file named @filename, with good error checking. If a file called @filename already exists it will be overwritten.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_charsets.html)- charsets
- Determines the preferred character sets used for filenames. The first character set from the @charsets is the filename encoding, the subsequent character sets are used when trying to generate a displayable representation of a filename, see g_filename_display_name().
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_display_basename.html)- display_ - basename
- Returns the display basename for the particular filename, guaranteed to be valid UTF-8. The display name might not be identical to the filename, for instance there might be problems converting it to UTF-8, and some files can be translated in the display.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_display_name.html)- display_ - name
- Converts a filename into a valid UTF-8 string. The conversion is
not necessarily reversible, so you should keep the original around
and use the return value of this function only for display purposes.
Unlike g_filename_to_utf8(), the result is guaranteed to be non-`None`
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_from_uri.html)- from_ - uri
- Converts an escaped ASCII-encoded URI to a local filename in the encoding used for filenames.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_from_utf8.html)- from_ - utf8
- Converts a string from UTF-8 to the encoding GLib uses for
filenames. Note that on Windows GLib uses UTF-8 for filenames;
on other platforms, this function indirectly depends on the
[current locale](https://gtk-rs.org/running.html#locale).
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_to_uri.html)- to_ - uri
- Converts an absolute filename to an escaped ASCII-encoded URI, with the path component following Section 3.3. of RFC 2396.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_to_utf8.html)- to_ - utf8
- Converts a string which is in the encoding used by GLib for
filenames into a UTF-8 string. Note that on Windows GLib uses UTF-8
for filenames; on other platforms, this function indirectly depends on
the [current locale](https://gtk-rs.org/running.html#locale).
- [find_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.find_program_in_path.html)- program_ - in_ - path
- Locates the first executable named @program in the user’s path, in the
same way that execvp() would locate it. Returns an allocated string
with the absolute path name, or `None``None`
- [format_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.format_size.html)- size
- Formats a size (for example the size of a file) into a human readable string. Sizes are rounded to the nearest size prefix (kB, MB, GB) and are displayed rounded to the nearest tenth. E.g. the file size 3292528 bytes will be converted into the string “3.2 MB”. The returned string is UTF-8, and may use a non-breaking space to separate the number and units, to ensure they aren’t separated when line wrapped.
- [format_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.format_size_full.html)- size_ - full
- Formats a size.

Return the inner pointer to the underlying C value.

Create a new font features tag attribute.

You can use this attribute to select OpenType font features like small-caps, alternative glyphs, ligatures, etc. for fonts that support them.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#features)`features`

a string with OpenType font features, with the syntax of the [CSS
font-feature-settings property](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-fonts-4/#font-rend-desc)

`pub struct AttrIterator<'list> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ AttrIterator](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrIterator.html) is used to iterate through a

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html)

`AttrList`A new iterator is created with [ AttrList::iterator()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html#method.iterator).
Once the iterator is created, it can be advanced through the style
changes in the text using

[. At each style change, the range of the current style segment and the attributes currently in effect can be queried.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrIterator.html#method.next_style_change)

`next_style_change()`## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

# AttrList in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.AttrList.html

`pub struct AttrList { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ AttrList](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html) represents a list of attributes that apply to a section
of text.

The attributes in a [ AttrList](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html) are, in general, allowed to overlap in
an arbitrary fashion. However, if the attributes are manipulated only through

[, the overlap between properties will meet stricter criteria.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html#method.change)

`change()`Since the [ AttrList](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html) structure is stored as a linear list, it is not
suitable for storing attributes for large amounts of text. In general, you
should not use a single

[for more than one paragraph of text.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html)

`AttrList`GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/attr_list.rs.html#46-48)

This function opens up a hole in @self, fills it in with attributes from the left, and then merges @other on top of the hole.

This operation is equivalent to stretching every attribute
that applies at position @pos in @self by an amount @len,
and then calling [ change()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html#method.change) with a copy
of each attribute in @other in sequence (offset in position
by @pos, and limited in length to @len).

This operation proves useful for, for instance, inserting a pre-edit string in the middle of an edit buffer.

For backwards compatibility, the function behaves differently when @len is 0. In this case, the attributes from @other are not imited to @len, and are just overlayed on top of @self.

This mode is useful for merging two lists of attributes together.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#other)`other`

another `AttrList`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#pos)`pos`

the position in @self at which to insert @other

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#len)`len`

the length of the spliced segment. (Note that this must be specified since the attributes in @other may only be present at some subsection of this range)

Serializes a [ AttrList](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html) to a string.

In the resulting string, serialized attributes are separated by newlines or commas. Individual attributes are serialized to a string of the form

`[START END] TYPE VALUE`Where START and END are the indices (with -1 being accepted in place
of MAXUINT), TYPE is the nickname of the attribute value type, e.g.
*weight* or *stretch*, and the value is serialized according to its type:

Optionally, START and END can be omitted to indicate unlimited extent.

- enum values as nick or numeric value
- boolean values as *true*or*false*
- integers and floats as numbers
- strings as string, optionally quoted
- font features as quoted string
- PangoLanguage as string
- PangoFontDescription as serialized by `FontDescription::to_str()`
- PangoColor as serialized by `Color::to_str()`

Examples:

```
0 10 foreground red, 5 15 weight bold, 0 200 font-desc "Sans 10"
0 -1 weight 700
0 100 family Times
weight bold
```
To parse the returned value, use [ from_string()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html#method.from_string).

Note that shape attributes can not be serialized.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-3)Returns

a newly allocated string

Update indices of attributes in @self for a change in the text they refer to.

The change that this function applies is removing @remove bytes at position @pos and inserting @add bytes instead.

Attributes that fall entirely in the (@pos, @pos + @remove) range are removed.

Attributes that start or end inside the (@pos, @pos + @remove) range are shortened to reflect the removal.

Attributes start and end positions are updated if they are behind @pos + @remove.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#pos-1)`pos`

the position of the change

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#remove)`remove`

the number of removed bytes

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#add)`add`

the number of added bytes

Insert the given attribute into the [ AttrList](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html).

It will replace any attributes of the same type on that segment and be merged with any adjoining attributes that are identical.

This function is slower than [ insert()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html#method.insert)
for creating an attribute list in order (potentially
much slower for large lists). However,

[is not suitable for continually changing a set of attributes since it never removes or combines existing attributes.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html#method.insert)

`insert()`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#attr)`attr`

the attribute to insert

Return the inner pointer to the underlying C value.

Create a new shape attribute.

A shape is used to impose a particular ink and logical
rectangle on the result of shaping a particular glyph.
This might be used, for instance, for embedding a picture
or a widget inside a [ Layout](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Layout.html).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#ink_rect)`ink_rect`

ink rectangle to assign to each character

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#logical_rect)`logical_rect`

logical rectangle to assign to each character

# Attribute in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.Attribute.html

`pub struct Attribute { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ Attribute](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Attribute.html) structure represents the common portions of all
attributes.

Particular types of attributes include this structure as their initial
portion. The common portion of the attribute holds the range to which
the value in the type-specific part of the attribute applies and should
be initialized using `Pango::Attribute::init()`. By default, an attribute
will have an all-inclusive range of [0,`G_MAXUINT`].

GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

# Color in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.Color.html

`pub struct Color { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

Fill in the fields of a color from a string specification.

The string can either one of a large set of standard names.
(Taken from the CSS Color [specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#named-colors),
or it can be a value in the form `#rgb`, `#rrggbb`,
`#rrrgggbbb` or `#rrrrggggbbbb`, where `r`, `g` and `b`
are hex digits of the red, green, and blue components
of the color, respectively. (White in the four forms is
`#fff`, `#ffffff`, `#fffffffff` and `#ffffffffffff`.)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#spec)`spec`

a string specifying the new color

# Context in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.Context.html

`pub struct Context { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ Context](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html) stores global information used to control the
itemization process.

The information stored by [ Context](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html) includes the fontmap used
to look up fonts, and default values such as the default language,
default gravity, or default font.

To obtain a [ Context](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html), use

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontMapExt.html#method.create_context)

`FontMapExt::create_context()`GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

Creates a new [ Context](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html) initialized to default values.

This function is not particularly useful as it should always
be followed by a [ set_font_map()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html#method.set_font_map) call, and the
function

[does these two steps together and hence users are recommended to use that.](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontMapExt.html#method.create_context)

`FontMapExt::create_context()`If you are using Pango as part of a higher-level system,
that system may have it’s own way of create a [ Context](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html).
For instance, the GTK toolkit has, among others,

`gtk_widget_get_pango_context()`. Use those instead.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

the newly allocated [ Context](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html), which should
be freed with g_object_unref().

Forces a change in the context, which will cause any [ Layout](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Layout.html)
using this context to re-layout.

This function is only useful when implementing a new backend for Pango, something applications won’t do. Backends should call this function if they have attached extra data to the context and such data is changed.

Retrieves the gravity for the context.

This is similar to [ base_gravity()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html#method.base_gravity),
except for when the base gravity is

[for which](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.Gravity.html#variant.Auto)

`Gravity::Auto`[is used to return the gravity from the current context matrix.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.Gravity.html#method.for_matrix)

`Gravity::for_matrix()`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-5)Returns

the resolved gravity for the context.

Gets the transformation matrix that will be applied when rendering with this context.

See [ set_matrix()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html#method.set_matrix).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-8)Returns

the matrix, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if no
matrix has been set (which is the same as the identity matrix).
The returned matrix is owned by Pango and must not be modified
or freed.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/context.rs.html#203-215)#### pub fn [metrics](https://gtk-rs.org#method.metrics)(
    &self,
    desc: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html)>,
    language: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[Language](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Language.html)>,
) -> [FontMetrics](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontMetrics.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/context.rs.html#203-215)

#### pub fn [metrics](https://gtk-rs.org#method.metrics)(
    &self,
    desc: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html)>,
    language: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[Language](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Language.html)>,
) -> [FontMetrics](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontMetrics.html)

Get overall metric information for a particular font description.

Since the metrics may be substantially different for different scripts, a language tag can be provided to indicate that the metrics should be retrieved that correspond to the script(s) used by that language.

The [ FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html) is interpreted in the same way as by

[, and the family name may be a comma separated list of names. If characters from multiple of these families would be used to render the string, then the returned fonts would be a composite of the metrics for the fonts loaded for the individual families.](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.itemize.html)

`itemize()`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#desc)`desc`

a [ FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html) structure.

[means that the font description from the context will be used.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#language)`language`

language tag used to determine which script to get
the metrics for. [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) means that the language tag from the context
will be used. If no language tag is set on the context, metrics
for the default language (as determined by

[will be returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Language.html#method.default)

**crate feature**only.

`v1_44`Returns whether font rendering with this context should round glyph positions and widths.

Returns the current serial number of @self.

The serial number is initialized to an small number larger than zero
when a new context is created and is increased whenever the context
is changed using any of the setter functions, or the [ FontMap](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontMap.html) it
uses to find fonts has changed. The serial may wrap, but will never
have the value 0. Since it can wrap, never compare it with “less than”,
always use “not equals”.

This can be used to automatically detect changes to a [ Context](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html),
and is only useful when implementing objects that need update when their

[changes, like](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html)

`Context`[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Layout.html)

`Layout`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-10)Returns

The current serial number of @self.

#### pub fn [set_matrix](https://gtk-rs.org#method.set_matrix)(&self, matrix: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[Matrix](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Matrix.html)>)

Sets the transformation matrix that will be applied when rendering with this context.

Note that reported metrics are in the user space coordinates before the application of the matrix, not device-space coordinates after the application of the matrix. So, they don’t scale with the matrix, though they may change slightly for different matrices, depending on how the text is fit to the pixel grid.

a [ Matrix](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Matrix.html), or

[to unset any existing matrix. (No matrix set is the same as setting the identity matrix.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`v1_44`Sets whether font rendering with this context should round glyph positions and widths to integral positions, in device units.

This is useful when the renderer can’t handle subpixel positioning of glyphs.

# Coverage in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.Coverage.html

`pub struct Coverage { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ Coverage](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Coverage.html) structure is a map from Unicode characters
to

[values.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.CoverageLevel.html)

`CoverageLevel`It is often necessary in Pango to determine if a particular
font can represent a particular character, and also how well
it can represent that character. The [ Coverage](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Coverage.html) is a data
structure that is used to represent that information. It is an
opaque structure with no public fields.

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# CoverageLevel in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/enum.CoverageLevel.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum CoverageLevel {
    None,
    Fallback,
    Approximate,
    Exact,
}
```
## Expand description

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.None)

### None

The character is not representable with the font.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Fallback)

### Fallback

The character is represented in a way that may be comprehensible but is not the correct graphical form. For instance, a Hangul character represented as a a sequence of Jamos, or a Latin transliteration of a Cyrillic word.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Approximate)

### Approximate

The character is represented as basically the correct graphical form, but with a stylistic variant inappropriate for the current script.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variant.Exact)

### Exact

The character is represented as the correct graphical form.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/font.rs.html#52-69)

**crate feature**only.

`v1_50`Loads data previously created via [ FontExt::serialize()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontExt.html#method.serialize).

For a discussion of the supported format, see that function.

Note: to verify that the returned font is identical to the one that was serialized, you can compare @bytes to the result of serializing the font again.

a `Context`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#bytes)`bytes`

the bytes containing the data

# FontDescription in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.FontDescription.html

`pub struct FontDescription { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html) describes a font in an implementation-independent
manner.

[ FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html) structures are used both to list what fonts are
available on the system and also for specifying the characteristics of
a font to load.

GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

#### pub fn [better_match](https://gtk-rs.org#method.better_match)(
    &self,
    old_match: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html)>,
    new_match: &[FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html),
) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Determines if the style attributes of @new_match are a closer match
for @self than those of @old_match are, or if @old_match is [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None),
determines if @new_match is a match at all.

Approximate matching is done for weight and style; other style attributes
must match exactly. Style attributes are all attributes other than family
and size-related attributes. Approximate matching for style considers
[ Style::Oblique](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.Style.html#variant.Oblique) and

[as matches, but not as good a match as when the styles are equal.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.Style.html#variant.Italic)

`Style::Italic`Note that @old_match must match @self.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#old_match)`old_match`

a [ FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html), or

Merges the fields that are set in @desc_to_merge into the fields in @self.

If @replace_existing is [ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), only fields in @self that
are not already set are affected. If

[, then fields that are already set will be replaced as well.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`If @desc_to_merge is [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), this function performs nothing.

corresponding values from @desc_to_merge, even if they
are already exist.

#### pub fn [set_absolute_size](https://gtk-rs.org#method.set_absolute_size)(&mut self, size: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html))

Sets the size field of a font description, in device units.

This is mutually exclusive with [ set_size()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html#method.set_size)
which sets the font size in points.

the new size, in Pango units. There are `PANGO_SCALE` Pango units
in one device unit. For an output backend where a device unit is a pixel,
a @size value of 10 * PANGO_SCALE gives a 10 pixel font.

#### pub fn [set_features](https://gtk-rs.org#method.set_features)(&mut self, features: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>)

**crate feature**only.

`v1_56`Sets the features field of a font description.

OpenType font features allow to enable or disable certain optional features of a font, such as tabular numbers.

The format of the features string is comma-separated list of feature assignments, with each assignment being one of these forms:

`FEATURE=n`where FEATURE must be a 4 character tag that identifies and OpenType feature, and n an integer (depending on the feature, the allowed values may be 0, 1 or bigger numbers). Unknown features are ignored.

Note that font features set in this way are enabled for the entire text that is using the font, which is not appropriate for all OpenType features. The intended use case is to select character variations (features cv01 - c99), style sets (ss01 - ss20) and the like.

Pango does not currently have a way to find supported OpenType features
of a font. Both harfbuzz and freetype have API for this. See for example
[hb_ot_layout_table_get_feature_tags](https://harfbuzz.github.io/harfbuzz-hb-ot-layout.html#hb-ot-layout-table-get-feature-tags).

Features that are not supported by the font are silently ignored.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#features)`features`

a string representing the features

The gravity field
specifies how the glyphs should be rotated. If @gravity is

This function is seldom useful to the user. Gravity should normally

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#size-1)`size`

the size of the font in points, scaled by `PANGO_SCALE`.
(That is, a @size value of 10 * PANGO_SCALE is a 10 point font.
The conversion factor between points and device units depends on
system configuration and the output device. For screen display, a
logical DPI of 96 is common, in which case a 10 point font corresponds
to a 10 * (96 / 72) = 13.3 pixel font.
Use [ set_absolute_size()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html#method.set_absolute_size) if you need
a particular size in device units.

`Style::Oblique`Most fonts will either have a italic style or an oblique style, but not both, and font matching in Pango will match italic specifications with oblique fonts and vice-versa if an exact match is not found.

#### pub fn [set_variations](https://gtk-rs.org#method.set_variations)(&mut self, variations: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)>)

**crate feature**only.

`v1_42`Sets the variations field of a font description.

OpenType font variations allow to select a font instance by specifying values for a number of axes, such as width or weight.

The format of the variations string is

`AXIS1=VALUE,AXIS2=VALUE...`with each AXIS a 4 character tag that identifies a font axis, and each VALUE a floating point number. Unknown axes are ignored, and values are clamped to their allowed range.

Pango does not currently have a way to find supported axes of
a font. Both harfbuzz and freetype have API for this. See
for example [hb_ot_var_get_axis_infos](https://harfbuzz.github.io/harfbuzz-hb-ot-var.html#hb-ot-var-get-axis-infos).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#variations)`variations`

a string representing the variations

Creates a string representation of a font description.

See [ from_string()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html#method.from_string) for a description
of the format of the string representation. The family list in
the string description will only have a terminating comma if
the last word of the list is a valid style option.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-14)Returns

a new string that must be freed with g_free().

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/font_description.rs.html#660-666)#### pub fn [from_string](https://gtk-rs.org#method.from_string)(str: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/font_description.rs.html#660-666)

#### pub fn [from_string](https://gtk-rs.org#method.from_string)(str: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html)

Creates a new font description from a string representation.

The string must have the form

`[FAMILY-LIST] [STYLE-OPTIONS] [SIZE] [VARIATIONS] [FEATURES]`where FAMILY-LIST is a comma-separated list of families optionally terminated by a comma, STYLE_OPTIONS is a whitespace-separated list of words where each word describes one of style, variant, weight, stretch, or gravity, and SIZE is a decimal number (size in points) or optionally followed by the unit modifier “px” for absolute size.

The following words are understood as styles: “Normal”, “Roman”, “Oblique”, “Italic”.

The following words are understood as variants: “Small-Caps”, “All-Small-Caps”, “Petite-Caps”, “All-Petite-Caps”, “Unicase”, “Title-Caps”.

The following words are understood as weights: “Thin”, “Ultra-Light”, “Extra-Light”, “Light”, “Semi-Light”, “Demi-Light”, “Book”, “Regular”, “Medium”, “Semi-Bold”, “Demi-Bold”, “Bold”, “Ultra-Bold”, “Extra-Bold”, “Heavy”, “Black”, “Ultra-Black”, “Extra-Black”.

The following words are understood as stretch values: “Ultra-Condensed”, “Extra-Condensed”, “Condensed”, “Semi-Condensed”, “Semi-Expanded”, “Expanded”, “Extra-Expanded”, “Ultra-Expanded”.

The following words are understood as gravity values: “Not-Rotated”, “South”, “Upside-Down”, “North”, “Rotated-Left”, “East”, “Rotated-Right”, “West”.

The following words are understood as color values: “With-Color”, “Without-Color”.

VARIATIONS is a comma-separated list of font variations of the form @axis1=value,axis2=value,…

FEATURES is a comma-separated list of font features of the form #feature1=value,feature2=value,… The =value part can be ommitted if the value is 1.

Any one of the options may be absent. If FAMILY-LIST is absent, then
the family_name field of the resulting font description will be
initialized to [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None). If STYLE-OPTIONS is missing, then all style
options will be set to the default values. If SIZE is missing, the
size in the resulting font description will be set to 0.

A typical example:

`Cantarell Italic Light 15 @wght=200 #tnum=1`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#str)`str`

string representation of a font description.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-15)Returns

a new [ FontDescription](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html).

Tries to cast to an object of type

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/object.rs.html#235)[§](https://gtk-rs.org#method.dynamic_cast_ref)#### fn [dynamic_cast_ref](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast_ref)<T>(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

# FontFamily in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.FontFamily.html

`pub struct FontFamily { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ FontFamily](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontFamily.html) is used to represent a family of related
font faces.

The font faces in a family share a common design, but differ in slant, weight, width or other aspects.

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

#### fn [dynamic_cast](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)<T>(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, Self>

`T`. This handles upcasting, downcasting
and casting between interface and interface implementors. All checks are performed at
runtime, while `upcast` will do many checks at compile-time already. `downcast` will
perform the same checks at runtime as `dynamic_cast`, but will also ensure some amount of
compile-time safety. [Read more](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/object/trait.Cast.html#method.dynamic_cast)

# FontMap in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.FontMap.html

`pub struct FontMap { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ FontMap](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontMap.html) represents the set of fonts available for a
particular rendering system.

This is a virtual object with implementations being specific to particular rendering systems.

This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#properties)Properties

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#item-type)`item-type`

# FontMetrics in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.FontMetrics.html

`pub struct FontMetrics { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ FontMetrics](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontMetrics.html) structure holds the overall metric information
for a font.

The information in a [ FontMetrics](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontMetrics.html) structure may be restricted
to a script. The fields of this structure are private to implementations
of a font backend. See the documentation of the corresponding getters
for documentation of their meaning.

For an overview of the most important metrics, see:

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

Gets the approximate character width for a font metrics structure.

This is merely a representative value useful, for example, for determining the initial size for a window. Actual characters in text will be wider and narrower than this.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/font_metrics.rs.html#62-64)#### pub fn [approximate_digit_width](https://gtk-rs.org#method.approximate_digit_width)(&self) -> [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)

#### pub fn [approximate_digit_width](https://gtk-rs.org#method.approximate_digit_width)(&self) -> [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)

Gets the approximate digit width for a font metrics structure.

This is merely a representative value useful, for example, for determining the initial size for a window. Actual digits in text can be wider or narrower than this, though this value is generally somewhat more accurate than the result of pango_font_metrics_get_approximate_char_width() for digits.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

the digit width, in Pango units.

Gets the ascent from a font metrics structure.

The ascent is the distance from the baseline to the logical top of a line of text. (The logical top may be above or below the top of the actual drawn ink. It is necessary to lay out the text to figure where the ink will be.)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-2)Returns

the ascent, in Pango units.

Gets the descent from a font metrics structure.

The descent is the distance from the baseline to the logical bottom of a line of text. (The logical bottom may be above or below the bottom of the actual drawn ink. It is necessary to lay out the text to figure where the ink will be.)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-3)Returns

the descent, in Pango units.

Gets the line height from a font metrics structure.

The line height is the recommended distance between successive baselines in wrapped text using this font.

If the line height is not available, 0 is returned.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-4)Returns

the height, in Pango units

# Fontset in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.Fontset.html

`pub struct Fontset { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ Fontset](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Fontset.html) represents a set of

[to use when rendering text.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Font.html)

`Font`A [ Fontset](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Fontset.html) is the result of resolving a

[against a particular](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontDescription.html)

`FontDescription`[. It has operations for finding the component font for a particular Unicode character, and for finding a composite set of metrics for the entire fontset.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Context.html)

`Context`This is an Abstract Base Class, you cannot instantiate it.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# FontsetSimple in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.FontsetSimple.html

`pub struct FontsetSimple { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ FontsetSimple](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontsetSimple.html) is a implementation of the abstract

[base class as an array of fonts.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Fontset.html)

`Fontset`When creating a [ FontsetSimple](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.FontsetSimple.html), you have to provide
the array of fonts that make up the fontset.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implements)Implements

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

# GlyphGeometry in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.GlyphGeometry.html

`pub struct GlyphGeometry { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The [ GlyphGeometry](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphGeometry.html) structure contains width and positioning
information for a single glyph.

Note that @width is not guaranteed to be the same as the glyph extents. Kerning and other positioning applied during shaping will affect both the @width and the @x_offset for the glyphs in the glyph string that results from shaping.

The information in this struct is intended for rendering the glyphs, as follows:

- Assume the current point is (x, y)
- Render the current glyph at (x + x_offset, y + y_offset),
- Advance the current point to (x + width, y)
- Render the next glyph

GLib type: Inline allocated boxed type with stack copy semantics.

# GlyphItem in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.GlyphItem.html

`pub struct GlyphItem { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/glyph_item.rs.html#8-23)#### pub fn [as_ptr](https://gtk-rs.org#method.as_ptr)(&self) -> [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[PangoGlyphItem](https://gtk-rs.org/pango_sys/struct.PangoGlyphItem.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/glyph_item.rs.html#8-23)

#### pub fn [as_ptr](https://gtk-rs.org#method.as_ptr)(&self) -> [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[PangoGlyphItem](https://gtk-rs.org/pango_sys/struct.PangoGlyphItem.html)

Return the inner pointer to the underlying C value.

Splits a shaped item ([ GlyphItem](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphItem.html)) into multiple items based
on an attribute list.

The idea is that if you have attributes that don’t affect shaping,
such as color or underline, to avoid affecting shaping, you filter
them out ([ AttrList::filter()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html#method.filter)), apply the shaping process
and then reapply them to the result using this function.

All attributes that start or end inside a cluster are applied to that cluster; for instance, if half of a cluster is underlined and the other-half strikethrough, then the cluster will end up with both underline and strikethrough attributes. In these cases, it may happen that @item->extra_attrs for some of the result items can have multiple attributes of the same type.

This function takes ownership of @self; it will be reused as one of the elements in the list.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#text)`text`

text that @list applies to

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#list)`list`

a `AttrList`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns)Returns

a
list of glyph items resulting from splitting @self. Free
the elements using `Pango::GlyphItem::free()`, the list using
g_slist_free().

Modifies @self to cover only the text after @split_index, and returns a new item that covers the text before @split_index that used to be in @self.

You can think of @split_index as the length of the returned item. @split_index may not be 0, and it may not be greater than or equal to the length of @self (that is, there must be at least one byte assigned to each item, you can’t create a zero-length item).

This function is similar in function to pango_item_split() (and uses it internally.)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#text-1)`text`

text to which positions in @self apply

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#split_index)`split_index`

byte index of position to split item, relative to the start of the item

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

the newly allocated item representing text before @split_index, which should be freed with pango_glyph_item_free().

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/glyph_item.rs.html#8-10)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/glyph_item.rs.html#12-14)

#### pub fn [glyph_string](https://gtk-rs.org#method.glyph_string)(&self) -> [GlyphString](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphString.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/glyph_item.rs.html#38-50)#### pub fn [logical_widths](https://gtk-rs.org#method.logical_widths)(&self, text: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)>

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/glyph_item.rs.html#38-50)

#### pub fn [logical_widths](https://gtk-rs.org#method.logical_widths)(&self, text: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)>

Given a [ GlyphItem](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphItem.html) and the corresponding text, determine the
width corresponding to each character.

When multiple characters compose a single cluster, the width of the entire cluster is divided equally among the characters.

See also [ GlyphString::logical_widths()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphString.html#method.logical_widths).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#text-2)`text`

text that @self corresponds to (glyph_item->item->offset is an offset from the start of @text)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-2)Returns

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#logical_widths)`logical_widths`

an array whose length
is the number of characters in glyph_item (equal to
`glyph_item->item->num_chars`) to be filled in with the resulting
character widths.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#trait-implementations)

# Item in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.Item.html

`pub struct Item { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/item.rs.html#54-58)#### pub fn [apply_attrs](https://gtk-rs.org#method.apply_attrs)(&mut self, iter: &mut [AttrIterator](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrIterator.html)<'_>)

**crate feature **`v1_44` only.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/item.rs.html#54-58)

#### pub fn [apply_attrs](https://gtk-rs.org#method.apply_attrs)(&mut self, iter: &mut [AttrIterator](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrIterator.html)<'_>)

**crate feature**only.

`v1_44`Add attributes to a [ Item](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Item.html).

The idea is that you have attributes that don’t affect itemization,
such as font features, so you filter them out using
[ AttrList::filter()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.AttrList.html#method.filter), itemize your text, then reapply the
attributes to the resulting items using this function.

The @iter should be positioned before the range of the item, and will be advanced past it. This function is meant to be called in a loop over the items resulting from itemization, while passing the iter to each call.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#iter)`iter`

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/item.rs.html#75-77)#### pub fn [char_offset](https://gtk-rs.org#method.char_offset)(&self) -> [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)

**crate feature **`v1_54` only.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/auto/item.rs.html#75-77)

#### pub fn [char_offset](https://gtk-rs.org#method.char_offset)(&self) -> [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)

**crate feature**only.

`v1_54`Returns the character offset of the item from the beginning of the itemized text.

If the item has not been obtained from Pango’s itemization machinery, then the character offset is not available. In that case, this function returns -1.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-1)Returns

the character offset of the item from the beginning of the itemized text, or -1

Modifies @self to cover only the text after @split_index, and returns a new item that covers the text before @split_index that used to be in @self.

You can think of @split_index as the length of the returned item.
@split_index may not be 0, and it may not be greater than or equal
to the length of @self (that is, there must be at least one byte
assigned to each item, you can’t create a zero-length item).
@split_offset is the length of the first item in chars, and must be
provided because the text used to generate the item isn’t available,
so `pango_item_split()` can’t count the char length of the split items
itself.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#split_index)`split_index`

byte index of position to split item, relative to the start of the item

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#split_offset)`split_offset`

number of chars between start of @self and @split_index

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-2)Returns

new item representing text before @split_index, which
should be freed with `Pango::Item::free()`.

# GlyphItemIter in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.GlyphItemIter.html

`pub struct GlyphItemIter<'item> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ GlyphItemIter](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphItemIter.html) is an iterator over the clusters in a

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphItem.html)

`GlyphItem`The *forward direction* of the iterator is the logical direction of text.
That is, with increasing @start_index and @start_char values. If @glyph_item
is right-to-left (that is, if `glyph_item->item->analysis.level` is odd),
then @start_glyph decreases as the iterator moves forward.  Moreover,
in right-to-left cases, @start_glyph is greater than @end_glyph.

An iterator should be initialized using either pango_glyph_item_iter_init_start() or pango_glyph_item_iter_init_end(), for forward and backward iteration respectively, and walked over using any desired mixture of pango_glyph_item_iter_next_cluster() and pango_glyph_item_iter_prev_cluster().

A common idiom for doing a forward iteration over the clusters is:

```
PangoGlyphItemIter cluster_iter;
gboolean have_cluster;
for (have_cluster = pango_glyph_item_iter_init_start (&cluster_iter,
                                                      glyph_item, text);
     have_cluster;
     have_cluster = pango_glyph_item_iter_next_cluster (&cluster_iter))
{
  ...
}
```
Note that @text is the start of the text for layout, which is then
indexed by `glyph_item->item->offset` to get to the text of @glyph_item.
The @start_index and @end_index values can directly index into @text. The
@start_glyph, @end_glyph, @start_char, and @end_char values however are
zero-based for the @glyph_item.  For each cluster, the item pointed at by
the start variables is included in the cluster while the one pointed at by
end variables is not.

None of the members of a [ GlyphItemIter](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphItemIter.html) should be modified manually.

# GlyphString in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.GlyphString.html

`pub struct GlyphString { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ GlyphString](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphString.html) is used to store strings of glyphs with geometry
and visual attribute information.

The storage for the glyph information is owned by the structure which simplifies memory management.

GLib type: Boxed type with copy-on-clone semantics.

Computes the logical width of the glyph string.

This can also be computed using [ extents()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphString.html#method.extents).
However, since this only computes the width, it’s much faster. This
is in fact only a convenience function that computes the sum of
@geometry.width for each glyph in the @self.

Converts from character position to x position.

The X position is measured from the left edge of the run. Character positions are obtained using font metrics for ligatures where available, and computed by dividing up each cluster into equal portions, otherwise.

## `text` the text for the run ## `length` the number of bytes (not characters) in @text. ## `analysis` the analysis information return from [`itemize()`][crate::itemize()] ## `index_` the byte index within @text ## `trailing` whether we should compute the result for the beginning ([`false`]) or end ([`true`]) of the character.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-4)Returns

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#x_pos)`x_pos`

location to store result

Convert from x offset to character position.

Character positions are computed by dividing up each cluster into equal portions. In scripts where positioning within a cluster is not allowed (such as Thai), the returned value may not be a valid cursor position; the caller must combine the result with the logical attributes for the text to compute the valid cursor position.

Given a [ GlyphString](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphString.html) and corresponding text, determine the width
corresponding to each character.

When multiple characters compose a single cluster, the width of the entire cluster is divided equally among the characters.

See also [ GlyphItem::logical_widths()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GlyphItem.html#method.logical_widths).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#length-1)`length`

the embedding level of the string

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-6)Returns

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#logical_widths)`logical_widths`

an array whose length is
the number of characters in text (equal to `g_utf8_strlen (text, length)`
unless text has `NUL` bytes) to be filled in with the resulting character
widths.

# HitPosition in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.HitPosition.html

`pub struct HitPosition { /* private fields */ }`## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/layout.rs.html#16-47)[§](https://gtk-rs.org#impl-HitPosition)### impl [HitPosition](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.HitPosition.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/layout.rs.html#16-47)

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#impl-HitPosition)

### impl [HitPosition](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.HitPosition.html)

The codepoint within the grapheme of the position.

This will always be either `0`, or the number of `char`s (*not bytes!*)
in the grapheme. This represents whether the user clicked near the start
of the grapheme or near the end; this is important for things like
resolving cursor positions.

# LayoutLine in pango - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/pango/struct.LayoutLine.html

`pub struct LayoutLine { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A [ LayoutLine](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LayoutLine.html) represents one of the lines resulting from laying
out a paragraph via

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Layout.html)

`Layout`[ LayoutLine](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LayoutLine.html) structures are obtained by calling

[and are only valid until the text, attributes, or settings of the parent](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Layout.html#method.line)

`Layout::line()`[are modified.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Layout.html)

`Layout`GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

Computes the logical and ink extents of a layout line.

See [ FontExt::glyph_extents()](https://gtk-rs.org/prelude/trait.FontExt.html#method.glyph_extents) for details
about the interpretation of the rectangles.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#logical_rect)`logical_rect`

Computes the height of the line, as the maximum of the heights of fonts used in this line.

Note that the actual baseline-to-baseline distance between lines
of text is influenced by other factors, such as

### impl [LayoutLine](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.LayoutLine.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/layout.rs.html#70-72)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/layout.rs.html#100-118)#### pub fn [x_to_index](https://gtk-rs.org#method.x_to_index)(&self, x_pos: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> [HitPosition](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.HitPosition.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/pango/layout.rs.html#100-118)

#### pub fn [x_to_index](https://gtk-rs.org#method.x_to_index)(&self, x_pos: [i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)) -> [HitPosition](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.HitPosition.html)

Converts from x offset to the byte index of the corresponding character within the text of the layout.

If @x_pos is outside the line, @index_ and @trailing will point to the very first or very last position in the line. This determination is based on the resolved direction of the paragraph; for example, if the resolved direction is right-to-left, then an X position to the right of the line (after it) results in 0 being stored in @index_ and @trailing. An X position to the left of the line results in @index_ pointing to the (logical) last grapheme in the line and @trailing being set to the number of characters in that grapheme. The reverse is true for a left-to-right line.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#x_pos-1)`x_pos`

the X offset (in Pango units) from the left edge of the line.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-8)Returns

[ false](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if @x_pos was outside the line,

[if inside](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`true`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#index_-1)`index_`

location to store calculated byte index for the grapheme in which the user clicked

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#trailing-1)`trailing`

location to store an integer indicating where in the grapheme the user clicked. It will either be zero, or the number of characters in the grapheme. 0 represents the leading edge of the grapheme.

Gets a list of visual ranges corresponding to a given logical range.

This list is not necessarily minimal - there may be consecutive ranges which are adjacent. The ranges will be sorted from left to right. The ranges are with respect to the left edge of the entire layout, not with respect to the line.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#start_index)`start_index`

Start byte index of the logical range. If this value is less than the start index for the line, then the first range will extend all the way to the leading edge of the layout. Otherwise, it will start at the leading edge of the first character.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#end_index)`end_index`

Ending byte index of the logical range. If this value is greater than the end index for the line, then the last range will extend all the way to the trailing edge of the layout. Otherwise, it will end at the trailing edge of the last character.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-9)Returns

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#ranges)`ranges`

location to
store a pointer to an array of ranges. The array will be of length
`2*n_ranges`, with each range starting at `(*ranges)[2*n]` and of
width `(*ranges)[2*n + 1] - (*ranges)[2*n]`. This array must be freed
with g_free(). The coordinates are relative to the layout and are in
Pango units.
